title: Veterans Pension Rate Redetermination — Countable Income After the Medical Deduction
content:
**Veterans Pension — medical deduction in a redetermined annual rate.**

The medical deduction is the medical figure, which is the insurance premiums counted plus the care cost, less the medical threshold when medical expense reports are on file, and nothing otherwise. The medical threshold is the rate category's 5 percent of its basic rate for the medical deduction, rounded to the cent: 872.00 for the no-dependent categories (basic rate 17440) and 1141.90 for the one-dependent categories (basic rate 22838).

Countable income after the medical deduction follows the deduction: when the deduction is positive and smaller than the countable income, the countable income less the deduction is used; when the deduction is positive and at least the countable income, no countable income is used; otherwise the countable income is used whole.

## Input — judgement — output

| Input | Judgement | Countable income used |
|---|---|---|
| no medical expense reports on file | deduction is nothing | whole |
| reports on file, medical figure at or below the threshold | deduction not positive | whole |
| reports on file, deduction positive and below countable income | partial | countable income less the deduction |
| reports on file, deduction positive and equal to or above countable income | full | 0 |

*Hypothetical:* no-dependent category, countable income 14000.00, medical figure 6872.00. Deduction 6000.00; countable income used 8000.00. With a medical figure of 14872.00 the deduction equals the income and none is used.
